On 15 September 2026, an Indian Navy vessel and a Pakistani naval vessel came into contact in the North Arabian Sea. India said the Pakistani vessel approached at high speed and manoeuvred unsafely while the Indian vessel was on a routine surveillance mission, and summoned Pakistan’s Chargé d’Affaires on 16 September to protest. Pakistan gave a different account, saying the incident occurred during its SEASPARK-26 naval exercise and alleging that the Indian vessel carried out aggressive manoeuvres near the Pakistani ship.
In this context, a video is being shared on social media (here, here) with the claim that it shows the collision between a Pakistani naval vessel and an Indian Navy warship on 15 September 2026. Let’s verify the truth behind the video in this article.
Claim: The video shows the collision between a Pakistani naval vessel and an Indian Navy warship on 15 September 2026.
Fact: The video does not show the collision between an Indian Navy warship and a Pakistani naval vessel on 15 September 2026. It shows a 2011 incident involving PNS Babur and INS Godavari during an escort mission for the merchant vessel MV Suez. Hence, the claim made in the post is Misleading.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to the same clip (archived) uploaded on a YouTube channel named “mix” on 16 October 2014. The video was titled “Pakistan Navy Ship BABUR VS Indian Navy Ship”, and its description stated that it showed a Pakistan Navy ship and an Indian Navy ship in the Gulf of Aden during the rescue of the merchant vessel MV Suez. This confirms that the video predates the recent collision by over a decade.
Using these clues, we searched for relevant keywords and found a 2011 NDTV report showing similar footage from another angle. According to the report, the collision occurred on 16 June 2011 when the Pakistani warship PNS Babur rammed into the rear of the Indian frigate INS Godavari while attempting to overtake it during an escort mission for the merchant vessel MV Suez. The report stated that PNS Babur, caught in INS Godavari’s wake in heavy sea conditions, scraped against the frigate and damaged its helicopter deck. It also showed footage recorded from the deck of PNS Babur, capturing crew members celebrating after the collision.
A press release issued by India’s Ministry of External Affairs on 18 June 2011 confirmed that India had formally protested Pakistan’s conduct, stating that PNS Babur’s risky manoeuvres jeopardised the safety of INS Godavari and its crew and violated international maritime safety regulations and the 1991 India-Pakistan agreement on advance notice of military exercises.
To sum up, this viral video shows a 2011 Pakistan-India naval collision, not the September 2026 incident.

A clinical trial by doctors at a private medical college hospital in Chickballapur near Bengaluru has found that a dual stellate ganglion block (SGB) procedure may help reduce anxiety symptoms in patients who do not respond to standard treatment.
The study, published in the July-August 2026 issue of Pain Physician, an open-access journal, involved 63 patients with moderate to severe treatment-resistant anxiety. The researchers found that those who underwent the procedure had a significantly greater reduction in anxiety symptoms than those who received a sham procedure.
What the study involved
Led by G. Niraj, senior consultant, anaesthesiology, and a multidisciplinary team of pain medicine physicians, psychiatrists, and clinical psychologists at the Sri Madhusudan Sai Institute of Medical Sciences and Research (SMSIMSR) in Chickballapur, the randomised controlled trial evaluated dual SGB specifically for treatment-resistant anxiety.
The study focused on patients whose anxiety had persisted despite standard treatment. Treatment-resistant anxiety was defined as failure to respond to at least one first-line medication and one first-line psychotherapy, each given for at least eight weeks. Most patients in the study had tried several medications. Forty-six of the 63 participants had tried at least two medications.
The study involved 63 patients, of whom 42 received the dual SGB procedure and 21 received the sham treatment. The patients were followed for 12 weeks.
What is the procedure?
A stellate ganglion block involves injecting a local anaesthetic and steroid mixture into a group of nerves in the neck under ultrasound guidance. These nerves are part of the sympathetic nervous system, which controls the body’s ‘fight-or-flight’ response.
The procedure was performed on both sides of the neck, with the second block given between 24 hours and seven days after the first. The researchers said that reducing excessive activity in the sympathetic nervous system may help ease some symptoms of anxiety.
“Persistent anxiety is not just in the head. The body’s stress alarm can remain stuck in the ‘on’ position. Our research helps to reset this stress response, offering hope to people whose anxiety has not responded to standard treatments,” Dr. Niraj said.
He stressed that SGB was not intended to replace psychological therapy or medication. “It provides another valuable option for patients with poorly controlled anxiety,” he said.
The procedure was generally well tolerated by the patients in the study. None of the adverse events reported in the SGB group was serious. Temporary hoarseness lasting one to three hours was reported by 14 patients, while one patient experienced numbness in an upper limb that resolved within six hours.
Future potential
Dr. Niraj and his colleagues said the findings could have implications for mental healthcare in both rural and urban areas, particularly where access to long-term psychological therapy is limited. The researchers said a clinic-based intervention, when used appropriately alongside existing mental health treatment, could provide a valuable option for patients with difficult-to-treat anxiety.
The researchers cautioned that the findings need to be confirmed through larger studies. The trial was conducted at a single centre and followed patients for only 12 weeks. Further research is needed to determine how long the benefits last and to better understand the mechanism through which SGB may help reduce anxiety.

Houthi attacks are driving up oil prices. For Yemenis in the crossfire, the toll is far greater
The lightning advance of the Iran-backed Houthi rebels has forced tens of thousands of people to flee their homes in Yemen
CAIRO -- As Houthi rebels closed in, Eshraq Abdel Gelil and her husband fled their home, walking through the mountains before catching a ride to a nearby city. Four months pregnant, she feared another miscarriage.
They are among more than 125,000 people who have fled as the Iran-backed rebels have advanced down the Red Sea coast to a key maritime chokepoint. The offensive, linked to the wider Iran war, has threatened Saudi oil exports, pushed up global fuel prices and rattled markets.
The cost has been far greater for Yemenis caught in the crossfire. Many have fled their homes with only what they could carry. The Arab world’s poorest country was pushed to the brink of famine in an earlier phase of the civil war, which killed an estimated 150,000 people.
A Saudi-led blockade, along with the Houthis’ repressive rule and detention of U.N. and aid workers, has made life miserable in the now-expanding territory under rebel control. Yemen’s Saudi-backed government, weak and fragmented, has struggled to push them back.
Abdel Gelil is now sheltering with family in the southwestern city of Taiz, while others are sleeping in the streets or erecting makeshift tents out of plastic.
Her husband, Mohamed Thabet, said the latest fighting was “extremely fierce” and more intense than a battle in 2017 that had also forced him to flee. “There was shelling and shrapnel near the house,” he said.
They walked for 5 kilometers (3 miles) before taking a vehicle for around 60 kilometers (37 miles) on mountain roads.
When they arrived in Taiz, a doctor told them that the baby had moved lower in the womb. Abdel Gelil miscarried at the same point in a previous pregnancy.
“My wife cried from the shock and was very fearful,” Thabet said.
Now they are packed into a home with extended family. They can only afford to eat twice a day, and they worry that Abdel Gelil is not getting enough nutrients for her and the baby.
Thabet also worries about his sister, who hasn't been able to afford her diabetes medication for over a month. She and her two daughters, 8 and 13, have a blood condition that makes them susceptible to anemia, he said.
The civil war dates back to 2014, when the Houthis seized much of northern Yemen, including the capital, Sanaa. Saudi Arabia intervened the following year in support of Yemen's internationally recognized government. A 2022 ceasefire largely halted the fighting.
Hostilities erupted again in July, when the Houthis renewed attacks on Saudi Arabia in what the rebels said was an attempt to lift the blockade. The attacks on Saudi Arabia's oil industry came as the U.S. was having some success in reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
The fighting in Yemen has killed eight civilians and wounded another 32, according to the U.N. humanitarian office, which says an estimated 125,000 people have fled their homes. The U.N. children's agency, known as UNICEF, says the displaced include more than 57,000 children.
“This is one of the most fast-moving and volatile displacement waves Yemen has seen in years,” said Obia Achieng, a UNICEF representative in Yemen. “Families are fleeing with little or no warning, often at night, carrying only what they can grab.”
“The situation is particularly concerning because it comes on top of an already severe humanitarian crisis,” Achieng added.
Before the latest fighting, the U.N. had warned that around 5 million Yemenis were experiencing “crisis or worse levels of acute food insecurity.”
Milena Murr, of Prosper Global, a humanitarian group previously known as Mercy Corps, said some people arriving in Taiz had walked for over 16 hours, arriving at displacement camps exhausted, dehydrated and with some of the children appearing malnourished.
Iman Abdullahi, country director for CARE, another aid group, said there's an urgent need for food, maternal and newborn healthcare, hygiene supplies, private latrines and mental health support.
“One woman had to wash her only clothes and remain inside her tent until they dried because she had nothing else to wear. Another was forced to flee just two weeks after giving birth,” he said.
Nashwan Ahmed Said was stitching together a tent from plastic wheat sacks. He said this is the third time he's been displaced since the start of the war.
“We are in such a state! We have no home, no toilet, no food and nothing to drink,” he said.
Arwa Ahmed, who was displaced with her five children, said she and her family ate nothing but rice for days.
“We need everything. We need tents, we need food and all the essentials, because we were displaced and took nothing with us,” she said.

I've recently introduced a few friends to the power of a great robot vacuum. One of my friends calls hers a marriage saver, while the other was both thrilled and horrified by how many stains the vacuum’s AI found on her floors. Personally, my robot vacuums keep me from wanting to set the litter box on fire, since my cat is on a mission to create his own navigational trail of litter through my home.
The best robot vacuums these days aren’t just vacuuming your floors, nor are they blindly bumping around your house like they used to. These gadgets are mopping, scrubbing away stains, lifting themselves off obstacles, and even reminding you to clean the dirtier areas in your home more frequently. A good robot vacuum can cost a pretty penny, but it doesn’t have to, depending on what you’re looking for. Curious about what’s the best model for you? I’ve been testing every new robot vacuum I can in my three-story home filled with three adults, a preschooler, and a cat who’s on a mission to get litter all over the house.
Here are the best robot vacuum cleaners I’ve tried this year, and everything we really liked from recent years. Looking for more vacuum ideas? Don't miss our guides to the Best Dyson Vacuums, Best Cordless Vacuums, Best Vacuums for Pet Hair, Best Carpet Cleaners, and Best Vacuums.
Updated September 2026: The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro is a new pick, and I've added testing notes on the Dreame L60 Ultra and Qrevo Curv 2, and updated notes on the Roborock Saros 20. I've also added a list of robot vacuum models announced at IFA 2026 that I plan to test this fall.
The Best Robot Vacuums
The Best Robot Vacuums of 2026
I’ve been testing the latest models from our favorite cleaning brands. Here are the top three I’d buy right now.
I was surprised how much I liked the AI-powered Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal. Its UV light revealed spots on my floor where I know I previously had spills, and its built-in AI had the vacuum go back over to deep-clean those spots in a way I clearly hadn’t done before. The UV Reveal also did a great job on my hard floors (both LVP and tile) as a mop-and-vacuum combo, as well as on my builder-grade carpet and a large rug in the living room. I was impressed that the rug actually felt just as fluffy and well-vacuumed as if I had cracked out my favorite Dyson stick vacuum instead of just sending a robot vacuum to do the work for me.
It has an extendable arm, which did a good job passing my corner test. I stuck three Cheerios in tricky corners of my home, and it got two out of three, doing better than the latest Dyson vacuum. It managed to get the trickier two corners too; it skipped the third Cheerio to avoid bumping my bar stools. I also did a spill test with two spots of cherry juice in my home. It mopped away the first spill with no problem, but I did have to send it back out to finish cleaning the second spill. The UV Reveal did great with obstacle avoidance and has “NeverStuck Technology” to lift itself off obstacles, and it worked to get itself off the flat, long legs of one of my side tables. The vacuum finished a cleaning run in a good amount of time, cleaning my entire main floor in about 60 minutes, but it does go back out to scrub all the spots it sees on the floor. That took another 30 minutes for me, but I assume that would get shorter over time, the longer you live with this vacuum and have it cleaning up. Still, 93 minutes to run through four rooms and go back to do some scrub work is a solid time window.
Overall, this vacuum really shines on hard floors, but I also liked it on rugs and carpet if you have a mix of these in your home. It has an auto-empty base with a bagless debris system, so you won’t need to worry about purchasing debris bags to empty the docking station. The only downside is that the vacuum can learn only a single map, so it doesn’t work for multiple floors of your home unless you’re game for it to remap every time (which takes only a couple minutes, so it’s not a horrible experience, but the vacuum will also want the base station lugged up or down the stairs too). The suction is also a mystery; Shark has declined to comment on the exact suction. Still, we’ve loved low-suction vacuums before, and the results have been great.

If you’re looking for vacuuming and mopping but don’t want to pay close to or beyond a four-figure sum, this is the vacuum to choose. Former WIRED editor Adrienne So previously recommended Eufy’s older X10 Pro Omni as a great robot vacuum without spending too much, and Eufy released the Eufy Omni C28 at the end of February with a similar set of features and price point. The Omni C28 comes with nearly double the suction power of the older model, a self-cleaning roller mop instead of mop pads, and retractable detangling brushes.
It does a solid job mopping and vacuuming, but it has a shorter battery life, leaving it at only 37 percent after completing the four-room main floor of my house. This is a bit of a bummer, since this affordable vacuum can do multi-floor mapping. While it can store enough maps to clean all three levels of my home, it doesn’t have the battery life to do so. But it does charge fairly quickly, and I was able to still clean all three floors of my house in a single day—I just had to let it recharge a little at the base first. It went back up to 57 percent battery life after just 20 minutes in its docking station. It also tried to eat the cords near my bed, and luckily I was nearby to yank them free. If you get this vacuum, make sure your cords are clear of the vacuum's reach.
With my corner Cheerio test, this vacuum also got two out of three Cheerios, but it missed the trickier fridge-corner Cheerio. This is the hardest spot to get into, so I’m not surprised, but it does mean you’ll have to check those corners more with this vacuum. The cherry juice spill test also showed similar results: the first spot it reached was cleaned completely, while the second spot, which had more time to dry, still had some sticky residue left behind.
Overall, though, it’s a good vacuum for the price, especially since it packs multi-floor mapping, the capability to mop and vacuum, and good results all around for a vacuum that’s already usually on sale for around $500.

If the Eufy isn't on sale (which is rare), I'd get this vacuum instead. The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro is the newest update to Roborock's more affordable Qrevo line that went without updates for years. The Qrevo 2 Pro is cheaper than the Curv 2 that launched back in January 2026 and still packs a ton of power, great navigation, and the same handy app. It comes with 20,000 Pa of suction, a FlexiArm mop that does a better job corner cleaning, and a reversible side brush to help dislodge corner debris.
It's technically the same price as the Eufy Omni C28, but the Eufy is usually on sale for a hefty discount. It's still early days for the Qrevo 2 Pro since it launched at the end of August, so if it starts going on sale more often, I'll label it as a true budget buy. (It has gone on sale once already and was a little cheaper than the Eufy.) There are a few contrasts to consider between the two similarly priced vacuums that came up in my testing. The Eufy got itself stuck on cords in my bedroom, while the Qrevo 2 Pro only attempted to eat cords without actually getting stuck on them. The Qrevo still isn't great at seeing small objects; it took my cat's toys for rides around the room, but they usually didn't get stuck or stop the vacuum.
Both scored a 2 out of 3 on my Cheerio test, but the Qrevo 2 Pro got the harder fridge Cheerio with its FlexiArm mop. However, the Eufy did better on mopping, cleaning most of the spills entirely. I'm giving the Qrevo 2 Pro a 1.25 out of 2—one spill was just about gone, but the area around it was all slightly sticky, while the second spill was only half cleaned. It's hard to perfectly grade. It also tends to leave some debris behind when it goes over thresholds that separate carpet from hard flooring, but it didn't have this issue when transitioning onto rugs.
But my favorite is how quiet this vacuum is. Both the base station and vacuum itself are quieter than the Eufy Omni C28, and it is especially pleasant if you let the Qrevo 2 Pro vacuum and mop separately. It takes longer than doing the combo cleans, but this vacuum pulled off doing both a separate vacuuming session and mopping of my massive first floor in two hours, which most vacuums still take for combo cleans. Overall it's a good vacuum, and it's especially worth snagging when on sale.

Honorable Mentions
There are a lot of great robot vacuums out there. Here are a few others we’ve tried and liked.
Dreame L60 Ultra for $1,300: This vacuum did a good all-around job and packs a ton of good features, including dual flex arms, the EasyLeap System that lets it move over almost-2-inch tall obstacles, and 35,000 Pa of suction. This is a great one to buy if you have tall thresholds in your home thanks to that lifting feature, but otherwise, you could get a smarter vacuum for a cheaper price. This vacuum does promise dirt detection, but I never noticed it delivering on that promise. Still, my Dreame long-term tester commented that it's leagues quieter than her older Dreame vacuum, so it's a good upgrade choice if you like Dreame and want something quieter.
Dreame X50 Ultra for $1,000: If you have pets that tend to make one area of your home particularly hair- or debris-covered, this is the vacuum to get. The Dreame X50 Ultra has tons of great features, including double-roll brushes, side wands for edge cleaning, and a large-capacity docking station, but the real standout is the AI that can notice extremely dirty areas. It’s the most effective dirt- and obstacle-identification system that former WIRED editor Adrienne So has tried, and it will even remind her which areas it needs to clean more often (for her, that’s near her dog’s bed).
Dyson Spot+Stain Ai for $1,200: The Dyson Spot+Stain Ai is a good robot vacuum overall, with a unique base station design that calls back to the Dyson stick vacuums and built-in AI to find spots and stains on your floor to scrub them away. It mostly worked, but I did prefer this feature in the Shark above, which has a similar starting retail price but is usually on sale. It’s also a little tall, so if you have builder-grade cabinets like I do, it might not be able to vacuum the toe kicks or underneath your Ikea furniture. (It got stuck underneath my Tolstad bed frame and was too tall to get underneath my Besta cabinet.)
iRobot Roomba Max 705 Combo for $799: The name Roomba is synonymous with robot vacuums for many people, but it’s actually a specific line made by iRobot. I really liked both the high-end look of the Max 705 Combo (not to be confused with the cheaper Max 705) and the overall job it did mopping and cleaning my floors. The app is great since it shows you a map of where the robot went, and it’ll also show you a little itinerary of which rooms it’s doing in what order. However, setup and any resetting you need to do is a long process, so be ready to commit when you unbox it.
Matic Robot Vacuum for $1,395: According to former WIRED editor Adrienne So, this vacuum is spectacular. It’s the only 10/10 rating she’s ever given a robot vacuum. Its six RGB infrared cameras do a great job making a 3D map, the single waste bag contains wet and dry debris, it does a great job cleaning toe kicks, and it was quiet enough to run without bothering So’s kids while they watched TV. That’s due to Matic’s lower suction power (only 3,200 Pa), but she didn’t notice any decrease in cleanliness as a result. It’s compact and square, giving it the ability to really get into corners. The only bummer is that it has expensive, proprietary waste bags. But those waste bags do have diaper salts, charcoal, and a HEPA filter, so you don’t have to replace the filters separately.
Narwal Flow for $1,250: WIRED’s Reviews team hasn’t always had success with Narwal’s vacuums, but when I tested this model late last year, I found it super easy to set up and get cleaning. I had no connectivity issues, installation was a breeze, and the app was easy to navigate. It did a good job cleaning my hard floors and rug, and even when I ran it right out of the box until it ran out of battery, it returned itself to its station to recharge and then resumed the task a few hours later, all on its own. The base station is also sleek and cute compared with the dark, bulky structures most have.
Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 for $1,000: This is another great option from Roborock and another part of the Qrevo line we've liked for years. The Qrevo Curv 2 came out in January and has similar strengths to the Qrevo 2 Pro above, but it has a roller mop called SpiraFlow instead of two individual mop pads. It also has similar struggles, with threshold debris and small objects being hard to spot. It's a good vacuum overall, and best on sale (which it often is!), but I'd pick my picks on sale over it.
What’s a Robot Vacuum?
A robot vacuum is an automated vacuum, usually shaped like a round disc, that moves around your house to vacuum (and mop, as many models these days include mopping) on your behalf. You might’ve heard some refer to these devices as “Roombas,” which is the brand that made the concept popular, but today just about every cleaning brand—from high-end Dyson to affordable Bissell—makes some kind of robot vacuum. They come with either a charging station or a larger docking station that can self-empty.
What Your Robot Vacuum Will Need
There are a few things most robot vacuums will need to work properly:
- Space around the base station. Many robot vacuum manuals recommend at least a foot of clearance on three of the four sides of the vacuum’s base station to ensure it has room to return home.
- A good Wi-Fi signal. If your robot vacuum connects to Wi-Fi, as many do these days for app control and software updates, it’ll need a strong connection wherever it’s placed. Most of them can only connect to the 2.4-GHz wireless band, so make sure you have that (and choose only that band when you’re setting up if your Wi-Fi shows those bands separately). Confused? Check out our guide to setting up your smart home.
- Regular maintenance. It might be a robot, but it can’t take care of itself. See below for my tips for basic robot vacuum maintenance, and make sure to read your vacuum’s manual to know what your specific model requires.
Are Robot Vacuums Going to Get Banned?
The Federal Communications Commission announced in late July that foreign-produced advanced robotic devices will now be included on the FCC’s Covered List. That list includes communications equipment and services that are deemed to pose an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States, and as of this week, that includes robot vacuums (and similar devices like robotic pool cleaners and lawn mowers). While it won’t ban any models already on the market that have FCC approval, we’ll likely see a huge decline in available new models after this year. Models made in the US will be fine, but future vacuums from popular brands like Dreame, Eufy, Roborock, and more could be affected. For now, you'll still see vacuums launching from these brands, though, since FCC approval is given months ahead of product launches.
This decision comes from an interagency body in the White House executive branch called the National Security Determination, which has deemed automated robotic devices a security risk due to the data they collect, which could be used for surveillance and be remotely commandeered by “malign actors.” While the initial documentation describes humanoid robots and a recent case of a humanoid robot’s cybersecurity vulnerability to be remotely taken over, the official description of these robot devices will include robot vacuums and any devices meeting the following criteria:
- Autonomous mobile robots that are capable of locomotion, obstacle avoidance, navigation, or movement on the ground
- Operates at a distance from a human operator or supervisor
- Combined weight of the device and docking station is over 4.4 pounds
- Contains a sensor capable of perceiving its environment
- Contains a component capable of providing network connectivity, including Bluetooth and Wi-Fi
- Contains software running locally or remotely, including firmware and AI or machine-learning model weights that control the robot’s navigation and movement perception
Overall, robot vacuums themselves aren’t banned, but new models from companies based outside the US won’t get FCC approval and can’t be sold in the US. You don’t need to stop using any robot vacuum you have, but if you’re in the market for a new one, it’s better to shop sooner before availability starts to decline—and prices are likely to rise as supply falls.
What’s New from IFA 2026?
A ton of robot vacuums were announced at IFA 2026, from vacuums that will be available this year to concept vacuums like the iRobot Duo. They're from brands all over the world and will be available here in the United States, as FCC approval was given before the new ban was announced. Here are a few that caught my eye that I plan to test in my home this fall:
Dyson R3 Nurovi Spot+Scrub UV for $1,199: Dyson's newest version of the Spot+Scrub is already here, but this time adds a UV light to help its AI spot stains. I'm excited to see how this one compares to my favorite Shark vacuum with similar features. It's due out this fall, so keep an eye out for my review.
Dyson R2 Nurovi Wash+Dry for $699: Dyson is also adding more budget-friendly robot vacuums to its lineup, and the R2 Nurovi Wash+Dry will both vacuum and mop for well under $1,000. It has triangular cleaning pads for getting into corners, as well as Dyson’s new Twin-capture system that promises more efficient debris removal.
Dyson R1 Nurovi Dry for $549: This is another, cheaper option from Dyson and is a true robot vacuum, with no mopping technology. Dyson says it's engineered for deep cleaning across hard floors and carpets with intelligent floor and dust sensing, and it has Dyson’s Twin-capture technology.
Eufy Omni E35 for $1,300: This robot vacuum is interesting to me as a parent, since it promises baby-grade cleaning with its Asthma & Allergy Friendly certification and TÜV-certified testing that shows 99.99 percent bacteria elimination. It also has 35,000PA suction and an updated self-cleaning roller mop, and washes with 140 degree Fahrenheit hot water (at the start, and the water does cool off as the robot moves through your home). It also adds stain detection and removal, which I'm looking forward to testing.
Roborock Saros 20 Flow for $1,700: While I'm currently testing the base Saros 20, the Saros 20 Flow is coming out next with roller mop technology instead of spinning mops, a retractable LiDAR turret (while the base Saros 20 doesn't have LiDAR), and 36,000 Pa of suction.
Roborock Qrevo 3 Edge Pro for $1,500: The Qrevo line continues to grow this year, and now the Qrevo 3 Edge Pro is added to the mix. (It'll be called the Saros 20 Neo in other countries.) It promises impressive threshold crossing with the ability to get itself over 3.46-inch obstacles thanks to the AdaptiLift Chassis 3.0, warm water mopping, and an impressive 36,000 Pa of suction. It'll also have the FlexiArm technology I've liked on other Qrevo models like the Qrevo 2 Pro. It's available now.
Other Robot Vacuums We’ve Tested
3i G10+ Robot Vacuum for $250: If you want a super-affordable vacuum with no docking station but still great specs, this is the one to get. It has shockingly powerful suction for the price point (18,000 Pa) and a 1-liter dustbin built into the vacuum. Former WIRED editor Adrienne So was particularly impressed with its navigation and how well it did at edge cleaning. It’s a mop, too, which is even more impressive at this price point. If you’re looking for cheap but still great, it doesn’t get better than this. However, it's currently only available used, and I'm keeping an eye out to see if it comes back in stock or is getting discontinued.
Eufy S2 for $1,600: This robot vacuum has an intense-looking base station. However, I was disappointed it missed both the fridge and bookshelf Cheerios in my corner test, giving it only a one out of three. Both cherry stains were scrubbed away, but the floor near where the stains were felt sticky all over even with the stains ostensibly wiped away. It’s especially a bummer given the price point.
Mova P10 Pro Ultra Gen2 for $523: This robot vacuum was solid, and especially did a good job with cleaning corners (it got a 2 out of 3 on the corner test, capturing both the stool and fridge Cheerios), but it did a poor job scrubbing away the cherry juice for my stain tests. One of the two stains was almost entirely left behind, and overall on casual runs of the vacuum it didn’t feel as if my floors were super clean. Still, if you’re looking for good corner cleaning, and carpets more than hard-floor deep cleaning, this is a solid robot vacuum for the price.
Roborock Saros 20 for $1,600: WIRED reviewer Adrienne So was mostly happy with this robot vacuum, as was I. She noticed the super-high suction (it hits 36,000 Pa) actually caused more debris to be left behind on her hard floors when it passed over thresholds; I didn't have this issue with thresholds, but I still found debris even immediately after having this vacuum clean my hard floors. It also only got a one out of three in my Cheerio test, which isn't great for such an expensive vacuum.
How I Test Robot Vacuums
I test all robot vacuums in my three-story townhouse, where they clean across luxury vinyl plank (LVP); tile; carpet; and a large, low-pile rug. I have a dining table and four barstools to navigate, and both a cat and a child who create daily messes. I run the vacuum at least three times across the main floors of my home to assess its overall performance and note any recurring issues or errors it encounters. I do pick up my son’s toys, but I like to watch how the robot navigates the various chair legs and side tables throughout my home, and whether it sucks up the power cords beside my bed. I also like to see how much battery life is left after a run is complete on each level of my home.
I also set up an obstacle course of sorts. The first one is the corner test, created by three Cheerios placed in three tricky corners on the middle floor of my home: one in the corner of an Ikea Billy bookshelf toe kick, one underneath my countertops next to the fridge, and one next to a barstool chair leg. It’s how I test how well each robot vacuum gets into corners and underneath cabinetry.
I also create intentional spills for these vacuums to clean up. I use maraschino cherry juice to create two spill spots, then use a paper towel to smear and thin the stain to better replicate a spill you might not have seen on your floors. Many robot vacuums have AI that promises to detect these kinds of stains, but so far, no vacuum has stopped and scrubbed both spots on its first try.
Frequently Asked Questions
Can You Use Robot Vacuums on All Kinds of Floors?
You can, especially since there are so many mopping models now to better clean hard flooring. You can use these devices on anything from hardwood to LVP and tile, though I wouldn't recommend leaving smaller rugs out for these autonomous gadgets to get stuck on. Large, set rugs are fine, but bathroom and kitchen mats or any thin, easily moved rugs should be cleared out of the way and put in the wash instead of vacuumed by your robot vac.
How Often Do You Need to Maintain Your Robot Vacuum?
Taking good care of your robot vacuum will help it last. Here’s the debris-removal process you should follow for each robot vacuum style.
- If it has a charger-only base: This means the debris is stored inside the vacuum. You’ll likely want to empty it after each use. If your vacuum has a fill line you can watch, you can empty it when it reaches that line, but after each use is really best practice.
- If it has a self-emptying docking station: Each manufacturer will have different advice about when a self-emptying station needs to be emptied, but it’s usually between 30 and 60 days, depending on design and use. If you run your vacuum daily and have a lot of debris, like pet hair, you might need to aim for 30 days or less.
- If it has water tanks: Dirty-water tanks should be cleaned after each mopping run of your vacuum. Clean water can stay filled in the station.
Make sure to review your robot vacuum’s manual for any other steps the manufacturer recommends you take regularly to keep the vacuum running for as long as possible. Many brands also have replacement parts, so you can swap out individual pieces like brushes without needing an entirely new vacuum.
Do I Still Need a Regular Vacuum if I Have a Robot Vacuum?
I recommend keeping some kind of vacuum on hand, though that can vary based on your home. If you have stairs, you’ll definitely still want a hand vacuum or stick vacuum that can easily maneuver and clean your staircase, while pet owners might want a vacuum that can clean upholstery. I prefer my Dyson stick vacuums for a good carpet clean, but your mileage may vary depending on your preferences. Either way, I think everyone needs a companion vacuum of some kind with a robot vacuum.
Do You Need a Self-Emptying Dock?
You don’t need it, but a self-emptying dock makes using a robot vacuum much easier. You aren’t fumbling with debris every time it runs, and having a single bag to remove or a bin to empty is much easier than pulling debris out of the vacuum itself. I’d even recommend choosing a stick vac with a self-emptying dock, as it just makes the whole experience so much easier.
How Does WIRED Obtain Robot Vacuums? What Happens When We’re Done Testing?
Almost all the robot vacuums we test are provided to us as press samples with the understanding that there is no guarantee of coverage or type of coverage. Most companies don’t want a used vacuum back, so we either donate them locally or have the top performers long-term tested to see how they last.

President Donald Trump threatened Wednesday to retaliate against Europe if the European Union follows through on a proposal to make Canada its first associate member.
The plan, floated earlier in the day by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, would deepen the EU's ties with Canada beyond their existing trade agreement.
Trump said he could respond with heavy tariffs or curb trade with Europe if he viewed the move as hostile, extending his trade fight with Canada to one of America's largest economic partners.
"If they do that, if I think it's at all a hostile act, I will put very serious tariffs or stop trading with Europe on many things," Trump told reporters after landing in North Carolina on Wednesday.
Trump called the prospect "laughable" and described Canada as a "terrible trade partner."
On Wednesday, Trump also issued a presidential memorandum directing federal agencies to identify Canadian-origin goods that could be removed from the federal procurement system, citing what his administration described as barriers facing US companies seeking Canadian government contracts.
At a rally on the same day, Trump said the US was "carrying the European nations with a $200 billion deficit," referring to the US goods deficit with the EU.
"All we have to do is say, you know what? We're not trading with you anymore. We don't need anything they have. We have cars, we have lumber, we have food, we have everything," Trump said.
Von der Leyen's proposed arrangement remains undefined: EU treaties do not currently provide for such a status, and officials have yet to spell out what rights or obligations it would carry.
Canada and the EU already have a broad trade agreement, the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement.
Von der Leyen said she wanted to build on it with a wider partnership spanning technology, energy, critical minerals, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, defense, and the Arctic.
After US-Canada trade talks broke down last month, Prime Minister Mark Carney moved to deepen Canada's commercial and security ties with Europe.
On Wednesday, his office said Ottawa had formally applied to join the British-led Joint Expeditionary Force, a rapid-response military partnership of 10 northern European NATO countries.

While the southwest monsoon has remained weak over power crisis-hit Keralam, electricity consumption has continued to soar in September, touching levels reminiscent of the summer months.
Consumption so far in September has averaged 93.6 million units (mu), which is arguably unprecedented for the southern State which is accustomed to cooler weather and lower State-wide electricity usage during the June-September southwest monsoon season. This is around 10 mu higher per day compared to the first 16 days of September 2025, show data with the Kerala State Electricity Board’s (KSEB) load dispatch centre.
This year, electricity consumption in September has stayed consistently above the 90 mu-mark on all days barring two Sundays when it dropped to 88.3 mu on September 6 and 89.12 on September 13.
In terms of electricity consumption, Sundays are generally considered lean days as most commercial, industrial and educational establishments tend to remain shut.
The highest consumption this month was recorded on September 11 which recorded a consumption of 96.39 mu. Meanwhile, Keralam is continuing to face heavy supply shortages during the evening hours when the demand is at its height.
According to a Thursday (September 17) morning update from the KSEB, the State experienced a shortage of 900 megawatts (MW) during the peak hours on Wednesday, forcing the utility to continue with Statewide power curbs. Although the KSEB has increased internal hydropower generation, electricity imports from outside the State remain the mainstay. Of the total consumption of 95.82 mu recorded on Wednesday, imports accounted for 71.06 mu. The peak demand stood at 4813 MW at 8.30 p.m.
So far during the current June-September southwest monsoon season, Keralam has recorded a rainfall deficit of 28% from the normal.
The KSEB has urged the public to shift electricity-guzzling chores such as ironing clothes, charging electric vehicles and using water pumps or washing machines to the day time when consumption is relatively on the lower side.
Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph had said on Wednesday that the State was exploring various avenues for securing emergency supplies to meet the demand. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan had said on Wednesday that the government intended to draw up plans for meeting the higher electricity demand anticipated during the period from October 2026 to June 2027.

Mark Carney said Canada will pursue a “unique security and economic alliance” with Europe as he positions his country as a base to build in the “new global economic order”.
Speaking to investors, company executives and government ministers at the inaugural Canada Investment Summit on Tuesday, the prime minister pitched Canada as a “safe harbour” and lucrative home for foreign capital as his government looks to reduce its reliance on trade with the United States.
Over the last 18 months, the relationship with the US has fractured, leaving Canada searching for ways to avert economic devastation.
“The world is becoming more divided and dangerous. Sovereignty and openness are now in tension. Economic integration is being weaponised. Tariffs are used as leverage,” Carney said – a nod to the Donald Trump’s penchant for trade levies.
“Canada recognised the rupture earlier than most. Our response reflects the two lessons we have taken from it: First, we must take care of ourselves, and second, we must take care of each other. Taking care of ourselves means building our strength at home and diversifying our partnerships abroad.”
While Carney has referred to the trade spat as a “war”, there was a duelling sense of optimism at the summit among senior Canadian officials that the country’s more global perspective could usher in hundreds of billions in fresh investment into the country.
That shift has been exemplified in recent weeks by Carney’s effort to strengthen Canada’s economic and political ties to the EU. Noting in his remarks at the summit that Canada is the only non-European member of Europe’s defence procurement initiative, the prime minister said his government will pursue a “unique” relationship with the bloc. He mused about the range of possibilities, including the prospect of visa-free travel and work between the two that has been raised in recent days, but said Canada and the EU were in early stage of talks.
Carney will be the guest of honour at the European parliament’s plenary meeting in Strasbourg this week. He will attend European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen’s annual state of the union speech on Wednesday, where she is expected to sketch out new areas for EU-Canada cooperation. On Thursday, Carney will address MEPs in von der Leyen’s presence. The commission president hastily changed her plans to stay in Strasbourg, after being criticised over her initial “unacceptable” decision to skip Carney’s speech and return to Brussels.
European officials are seeking to bring Canada as close as possible to the EU short of membership. But it will not be called associate membership, as the EU seeks to maintain a clear distinction between members and nonmembers. The long experience of Brexit negotiations cemented the EU’s preference not to split the four freedoms of its single market – free movement of people, services, goods and capital – so any deepening of the Canada relationship will be built around this red line. More immediately, the EU hopes to improve ties on raw materials and energy.
Javier Moreno Sánchez, a Spanish socialist MEP, who leads the European parliament’s Canada delegation, said he wanted to hear “concrete steps” from von der Leyen on how to improve the EU-Canada relationship, calling for greater mobility for professionals, more student exchanges, joint work on defence and artificial intelligence.
“Canadians are the most European people outside Europe and that is the key point for the development of our relationship,” he said. “Due to the difficult geopolitical geoeconomic situation in the world and the difficult relationship we have, both Canada and the European Union, with our traditional partner, the United States, I think it is the moment to have a closer relationship with Canada.”
The EU and Canada already have a wide-ranging relationship, including a free-trade agreement and separate deals on digital cooperation, raw materials, research and a shared green alliance. Earlier this year, Canada became the first non-European country to join the EU’s €150bn defence loans scheme, meaning greater opportunities for Canadian defence firms to supply Europe.
But irritants persist. Ten EU member states, including France, Italy and Poland, have not ratified the landmark EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (Ceta) nearly a decade after it was signed, meaning parts of the deal are yet to enter into force.
French lawmaker Valérie Hayer, Emmanuel Macron’s ally in the European parliament, acknowledged the problem. “In the French parliament this agreement has yet to be ratified, notwithstanding the [trade] figures which are extremely good. That is why I call on political leaders [in France] to do their bit to act responsibly as elsewhere to make sure that we [the EU] can count for more in world affairs.”
Hayer’s centrist Renew group, only the fifth-largest in the European parliament, is calling on EU member states and the commission to speed up Ceta ratification and launch an awareness-raising drive so European and Canadian companies have better knowledge of the trade opportunities. But ahead of a year of big elections – in France, Italy and Poland – progress on ratifying the 10-year-old agreement looks uncertain.
EU-Canada’s trade in goods and services hit €130bn in 2025, an 80% increase since 2016 when Ceta was signed. But this pales in comparison to trade with the US, which is worth nearly US$880bn.
Despite a deliberate push to increase global trade, Carney acknowledged the geographic realities of Canada’s proximity to its southern neighbour, and the reality, which most economists concede, that the US will remain Canada’s largest trading partner.
“We will always be neighbours, and Canada will continue to be the US’s most important partner in many key areas,” he said. These arrangements work when we engage as true partners that respect each other’s traditions and sovereignty.”
In recent weeks, Trump has both threatened Canada’s economy and mused about a North America under the umbrella of an expanded US.
Event host Erik Schatzker told attendees that Canada was neither a “bystander nor a victim” in the dramatic geopolitical shifts that have defined the Trump era. “Canada is a protagonist. Canada has agency. Canada is defining its own future.”
Carney said foreign investment has dramatically increased and the federal government was on track to balance the operating budget one year ahead of schedule, an announcement that received applause from the crowd. He announced a corporate tax “mega-deduction” that would help compete with similar incentives in the US allowing companies to immediately deduct 100% of the cost of new investment across more assets than previously permitted.
Carney also confirmed Canada would open four of its major airports to foreign investment in order to “unlock their true value”. The prime minister also said his government would “apply [the] lessons” of instances in which allowing partial private investment had failed.
But that theme – soliciting hundreds of billions in foreign investment while also reshoring domestic capability – has frustrated some.
Ahead of the summit, thousands gathered in downtown Toronto for the Many vs the Money counter protest. Organisers said public money should not be used to reduce the risks of private investment while communities are left to shoulder the social and environmental costs of these projects.
“Mark Carney’s here selling Canada to the international community,” said Stephen Hill, a lone protester standing outside the hotel as key figures arrived to the prime minister’s speech. “I’m Canadian. We’re an Aboriginal-led investment coalition. We want in. But you can’t get a returned email. You can’t get a returned phone call. You can’t get through to his ministers. So I’m here from British Columbia to try and get his attention and to tell him to think of Canadians first.”
Ahead of Tuesday’s summit, the prime minister’s office announced nearly C$500bn in new domestic investment.
“Canada has what the world wants,” Carney said during media availability late Tuesday morning. “The difference, this week, is that we didn’t cross an ocean to make our case. The world came to us … but what matters most is what we do for ourselves.”

PM Mementos e-auction: 1,498 gifts to go under the hammer from September 17
Ministry of culture to launch the PM Mementos e-auction on September 17, putting up 1,498 gifts received by Prime Minister Narendra Modi for public bidding
The ministry of culture will launch the eighth edition of the PM Mementos e-auction on September 17, putting up 1,498 gifts received by Prime Minister Narendra Modi for public bidding.
The collection includes 50 objects identified as “hero objects” this year, with a silver memento of Lord Ram from Karnataka carrying the highest base price of ₹13.50 lakh. It is followed by a silver replica of the Kakatiya Kala Thoranam priced at ₹9 lakh, a framed Gond art painting titled “Tree of Life” priced at ₹7.50 lakh, a Jagannath Parivar piece mounted on a chariot with a base price of ₹6 lakh, and a 99.99% fine gold-plated framed Radha Krishna artwork priced at ₹5.40 lakh.
Union culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat on Wednesday said the initiative reflected the Prime Minister’s personal approach to public service. “The Prime Minister has never worked in self interest. He truly believes in and embodies the fact that what the country has given him is not his to keep but has to be returned to people,” Shekhawat said.

The items have been sourced from across the country. States such as West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Assam, Bihar and Odisha account for the larger share of the collection, the ministry said. Tezpur University student found dead in hostel room, suicide suspected: Assam police
A 20-year-old BSc student from Assam’s Tezpur University was found hanging in his hostel room on Wednesday. Police suspect suicide.
A 20-year-old student of Assam’s Tezpur University was found dead in his hostel room on the university campus on Wednesday afternoon, with police suspecting suicide.
Sonitpur senior superintendent of police (SSP) Barun Purkayastha said the Bachelor of Science (BSc) student was found hanging in his hostel room, with the door locked from inside.
“We received the information at around 1:30pm. The body was recovered by our team and it was sent to the Kanaklata Civil Hospital (KCH), where the doctors confirmed the death before the postmortem was conducted,” he said.
Registrar of the university Chandan Goswami told HT that the deceased was a resident of Nagaon district and was pursuing a BSc in the Integrated Chemistry department.
“He was sharing a room with another student who went to class in the morning. When the roommate returned around 1:30pm, he found the room locked from inside and, through the ventilator, saw his fellow student hanging,” Goswami said.
Police officers said a diary was found, but its contents could not be shared as the matter was under investigation.
The SSP said the family members of the deceased were asked to come to Tezpur after the incident and that the body was handed over to them around 7pm on Wednesday.
“We are investigating the matter and the university authorities are cooperating with us,” SSP Purkayastha said, adding that statements of other students and staff familiar with the incident would be recorded as per the law.

The chair of a congressional committee trying to pry non-disclosure agreements from billionaire Leon Black for its Jeffrey Epstein investigation proposed a bill on Wednesday that would allow victims of sexual abuse to break NDAs.
Rep. James Comer announced the bill a day after the House Oversight Committee unanimously voted for a resolution to hold Black, the Epstein associate and former CEO of Apollo Global Management, in contempt of Congress for refusing to comply with a subpoena requiring him to hand over all of his NDAs, and any in his possession that reference Epstein or Ghislaine Maxwell.
"During our investigation, we've learned how powerful men weaponized nondisclosure agreements to silence survivors of sexual abuse," Comer, a Kentucky Republican, said in a statement Wednesday. The proposed bill would ensure that sexual-abuse survivors and other people with information about such abuse could speak freely about it, he said.
Business Insider reported earlier this year that some of Epstein's accusers have signed confidential settlements with friends of Epstein whom they have also accused of misconduct, according to three people with direct knowledge of such settlements. The settlements include NDAs, the people said. One person told Business Insider they had direct knowledge of settlements with four of Epstein's friends who were accused of sexual misconduct by more than 20 women between them.
The House Oversight Committee in June issued two subpoenas to Black when he refused to answer questions about NDAs in a closed-door interview about his interactions with Epstein. Black, who gave over $150 million to Epstein for what he said were financial services, walked out of that voluntary interview.
This month, Black sued the committee rather than comply with the subpoenas. One subpoena demanded NDAs; the other required him to testify under oath in a deposition.
Epstein died in 2019 while awaiting trial for federal sex-trafficking charges. Maxwell was sentenced to 20 years in prison after a Manhattan jury found her guilty in 2021 of trafficking girls to Epstein for sex.
Black has said he wasn't aware of Epstein's sexual abuse of women. His lawsuit says the committee didn't have a "valid legislative purpose" for "such a sweeping and intrusive subpoena served upon a private citizen."
If passed into law, the proposed bill, called the Survivor's Voice Protection Act, would void nondisclosure clauses if they prohibit victims of sexual abuse from disclosing those experiences, or if they bar any other person from disclosing facts related to such abuse. The law would also create a fiduciary duty to inform law enforcement about suspected sexual grooming of minors.
Democrats on the House Oversight Committee have not yet said whether they would support the law.
The House of Representatives hasn't scheduled a vote on whether to hold Black in contempt of Congress. Black's lawyers called the Oversight committee's resolution "a complete abomination."
"This is retaliation — plain and simple," attorneys Susan Estrich and Aaron Cutler said in a statement. They said the subpoenas were "illegitimate, illegal, and a textbook abuse of power designed to bully and destroy legal protections of private citizens."
People with non-disclosure agreements can be legally compelled to speak about their experiences with a subpoena, but not in a voluntary interview with Congress. Some of Epstein's other associates, including Bill Gates, said in voluntary interviews that they didn't sign any non-disclosure agreements with Epstein or Maxwell victims.
Many states banned NDAs related to sexual abuse during the #MeToo movement following reporting about Harvey Weinstein, but no such ban exists on a federal level.

Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled Chile’s bloody 1970s political strife and its subsequent social and political turmoil in films such as The Battle of Chile and Nostalgia for the Light, has died aged 85. According to Chilean news outlet Emol, Guzmán died on Tuesday in Paris after a cardiorespiratory arrest.
Guzmán’s chief preoccupation throughout his career was the carnage unleashed by Augusto Pinochet’s coup in 1973 against Salvador Allende, Chile’s elected president. He later told the Guardian: “I’m a film-maker who was very marked by the ways of the dictator. It has remained with me for ever. I cannot leave it behind.” However, he resisted the idea that he was an activist, political film-maker, adding: “I’m not a sociologist. Neither am I a politician. I make films that are metaphorical and poetic; I interpret reality through my own personal way of looking.”
Born in Chile in 1941, Guzmán initially worked in advertising before studying film, first in Chile and then in Madrid. On his return to Chile, Guzmán responded to the febrile political atmosphere after Allende’s election in 1970, eventually completing the mammoth Battle of Chile documentary that chronicled Pinochet’s ultimately successful attempt to overthrow Allende, resulting in the latter’s suicide. Guzmán did not shrink from the brutality of the period, even including footage shot by camera operator Leonardo Henrichsen as he is shot dead by the soldier he is filming.
Guzmán was helped in the endeavour by French film-maker Chris Marker, who supplied film stock and connections that proved vital to make the film. Guzmán himself was arrested but eventually released, but the film’s cinematographer Jorge Müller was not so lucky – along with his girlfriend Carmen Bueno, he was arrested, tortured and “disappeared” in 1974.
Guzmán completed The Battle of Chile outside the country, releasing each of its three parts – The Insurrection of the Bourgeoisie (1975), The Coup d’État (1976) and Popular Power (1979) – through the rest of the 70s. Described by the Guardian as “an outstandingly photographed example of a newsreel film that captures the drama and volatility of the period”, it has continued to attract acclaim since then. Guzmán revisited the film in the mid-90s with Chile, Obstinate Memory, in which he returned to the country after a quarter-century of exile. In 2001 he completed The Pinochet Case, after the Chilean former dictator was arrested in London in 1998.
The director moved on to more metaphysical subjects with a trilogy of films starting in 2010: Nostalgia for the Light, The Pearl Button and The Cordillera of Dreams. They sought to explore Chile’s traumatic past by absorbing the country’s magnificent natural landscapes. His final film, My Imaginary Country, was premiered in 2022 and covered Chile’s dramatic 2019 street protests.

ఆల్ఫాజియో (AlphaGeo) సంస్థ నిర్వహించిన అధ్యయనం ప్రకారం, ప్రకృతి విపత్తులను ఎదుర్కోవడంలో తెలంగాణ రాజధాని హైదరాబాద్ ప్రపంచంలోనే రెండో అత్యంత బలహీనమైన నగరంగా నిలిచిందని, పెరుగుతున్న ఉష్ణోగ్రతలు, తీవ్రమైన వర్షాలు, వరదలను తట్టుకునే స్థాయిలో నగర మౌలిక వసతులు లేవని పేర్కొంటూ ఓ పోస్టు సోషల్ మీడియాలో (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ & ఇక్కడ) వైరల్ అవుతోంది. ఈ కథనం ద్వారా అందులో ఎంత నిజముందో చూద్దాం.
క్లెయిమ్: ఆల్ఫాజియో అధ్యయనం ప్రకారం, ప్రకృతి విపత్తులను ఎదుర్కోవడంలో తెలంగాణ రాజధాని హైదరాబాద్ ప్రపంచంలో రెండో అత్యంత బలహీనమైన నగరంగా నిలిచింది.
ఫాక్ట్(నిజం): ఆల్ఫాజియో అధ్యయనం భారతదేశంలోని హైదరాబాద్ను ప్రకృతి విపత్తులను ఎదుర్కోవడంలో ప్రపంచంలో రెండో అత్యంత బలహీనమైన నగరంగా పేర్కొనలేదు. ఈ అధ్యయనంలో పాకిస్తాన్లోని హైదరాబాద్ నగరం 41 రెసిలెన్స్-అడ్జస్టెడ్ రిస్క్ (RAR) స్కోరును పొందింది, ఇది విశ్లేషించిన ప్రధాన నగరాల్లో ఆరు అత్యంత తక్కువ ప్రకృతి విపత్తును తట్టుకోగల నగరాల్లో ఒకటిగా నిలిచింది. కావున పోస్టు ద్వారా చెప్పేది తప్పు.

ఆల్ఫాజియో తన క్లైమేట్ రిస్క్ & రెసిలెన్స్ ఇండెక్స్ (CRRI)ను ఉపయోగించి ప్రపంచంలోని 72 అతిపెద్ద నగరాలను విశ్లేషించింది. ఈ సూచిక వరదలు, అధిక ఉష్ణోగ్రత, కరువు, కార్చిచ్చులు, తుఫాను గాలులతో సహా ఆరు భౌతిక వాతావరణ ప్రమాదాలను అంచనా వేస్తుంది. ఈ అధ్యయనం ప్రకారం, పాకిస్తాన్లోని హైదరాబాద్ 41 రెసిలెన్స్-అడ్జస్టెడ్ రిస్క్ (RAR) స్కోరును పొందింది, ఇది విశ్లేషించిన ప్రధాన నగరాల్లో ఆరు అత్యంత తక్కువ ప్రకృతి విపత్తును తట్టుకోగల నగరాల్లో ఒకటిగా నిలిచింది. అయితే, ప్రకృతి విపత్తులను ఎదుర్కోవడంలో భారతదేశంలోని హైదరాబాద్ ప్రపంచంలో రెండో అత్యంత బలహీనమైన నగరంగా ఈ అధ్యయనం పేర్కొనలేదు.
అత్యధిక ప్రమాదం ఉన్న నగరాల జాబితాలో RAR స్కోరు 41తో అహ్మదాబాద్ (భారతదేశం) మొదటి స్థానంలో, 41తో హైదరాబాద్ (పాకిస్తాన్) రెండో స్థానంలో, 38తో ముల్తాన్ (పాకిస్తాన్) మూడో స్థానంలో, 36తో ఢాకా (బంగ్లాదేశ్) నాలుగో స్థానంలో, 35తో కోల్కతా (భారతదేశం) ఐదో స్థానంలో, 35తో లాహోర్ (పాకిస్తాన్) ఆరో స్థానంలో నిలిచాయి. మరోవైపు, RAR స్కోరు 8తో చికాగో అత్యంత తట్టుకునే సామర్థ్యం ఉన్న ప్రధాన నగరంగా మొదటి స్థానంలో నిలిచింది.
చివరిగా, ఆల్ఫాజియో అధ్యయనంలో ప్రకృతి విపత్తులను ఎదుర్కోవడంలో రెండో అత్యంత బలహీనమైన నగరంగా నిలిచింది  పాకిస్తాన్లోని హైదరాబాద్, తెలంగాణ రాజధాని హైదరాబాద్ కాదు.

Jadavpur University (JU) saw night-long rampage and vandalism on August 20, when a mob, armed with sticks and rods, allegedly stormed the campus.
The violence followed a heated altercation late on August 19 between activists from the Akhil Bharaitya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) from the university’s engineering department and members of the Left-wing student outfit, Democratic Students’ Federation (DSF), and other student organizations. The ABVP alleged that its members were assaulted and that several workers required hospitalisation. Students from the engineering faculty disputed the claim and offered a counter-account of the incident.
By midnight, an armed mob allegedly entered the campus, apparently seeking to avenge the earlier altercation. The attackers tore down and set fire to placards, festoons and flags belonging to various student organisations active on the campus. The mob also surrounded Aurobindo Bhavan, the university’s administrative building, trapping students inside.
The violence was captured by CCTV cameras installed across the university campus. Students and journalists also recorded several videos of the incident. Alt News accessed multiple such recordings and analysed them to establish the identities of those involved in the ruckus.
What happened at JU: A Blow-by-Blow Account
Around 9:30–10:30 pm on August 19, the DSF-run Faculty of Engineering & Technology Students’ Union (FETSU) held a general body meeting on the campus. The meeting had been announced through the union’s social media account.
ABVP and the allied Right-wing student outfit, Nationalist Students’ Front (NSF), opposed the meeting, citing a Calcutta high court ruling that no activities could be undertaken from student union offices until fresh student union elections were held. According to students present, ABVP and NSF members were outnumbered and were forced to leave the spot. A few DSF members were also injured in the ensuing scuffle.
Ayantik Pal, a third-year B Tech student who attended the meeting, said the GB meeting had been convened to elect signatories for the union’s email ID, Facebook account and bank account. Since the last FETSU election was held in 2020, he said, the meeting was intended to allow the union to continue its functioning.
According to Pal, ABVP activists at the meeting repeatedly objected that it was illegal. He said they nevertheless participated when names for the signatories were being proposed, before becoming agitated as the meeting progressed. They allegedly abused some students, calling them “Naxals” and “Maoists”, following which a scuffle broke out.
Accounts diverge over what happened immediately afterwards.
According to students, Nikhil Das, an ABVP research scholar and president of the organisation’s JU unit, attempted to enter the undergraduate and postgraduate students’ GB meeting and allegedly tried to provoke a confrontation. Students said they intervened to stop him, escalating the situation. They alleged that three DSF workers were injured in the assault by ABVP activists and that one was taken away towards the Sulekha Crossing. ABVP denied these allegations.
ABVP, meanwhile, claimed that Das was assaulted during the GB meeting and subsequently had to be hospitalised at KPC Medical College and Hospital. BJP MLA from Jadavpur Sarbari Mukherjee visited him at the hospital. Students alleged that during the visit, she threatened that ABVP and BJP workers would retaliate if those accused in the assault did not surrender. She later repeated this on camera.
Around midnight, a crowd of approximately 50–60 people gathered outside Gate 4 of the university, which is the only entrance that remains open at night. By around 12:30 am, the group entered the campus.
Pramita Basu, an undergraduate Philosophy student, said that after 7 pm, everyone entering the campus is required to show an ID card, including hostel residents. However, according to her, the crowd entered without being stopped by the guards stationed at the gate.
The group moved from Gate 4 towards the Science-Arts crossing, where some wall graffiti was allegedly damaged, before turning towards Aurobindo Bhavan, the university’s administrative building. Videos from the night accessed by Alt News show some members of the group carrying saffron flags.
Meanwhile, students who had remained on campus after the earlier confrontation gathered inside Aurobindo Bhavan. According to them, they had decided to stay back until morning because they had heard that ABVP activists were looking for them outside the university.
Pal said an all-faculty GB meeting was also convened that night, with students from the arts, science and engineering faculties discussing what to do next. Around 12:30 am, he said, a university staff member alerted them that a mob had entered the campus and advised them to protect themselves.
“Within minutes, we saw a stream of mobile flashlights coming towards Aurobindo Bhavan from the side of the green zone. A few students present at the green zone were thrashed by this mob,” Pal said.
The students then woke the guards at Aurobindo Bhavan, obtained the keys and locked themselves inside, according to Pal.
The crowd that reached the building tried to break through its collapsible gates but failed. It then tore down red flags, festoons and posters belonging to student organisations and set them on fire outside the administrative building. Students trapped inside alleged that members of the crowd abused them verbally, threw stones and eggs at the building, and attempted to throw burning flags inside. Footage of the episode was broadcast live on television and recorded by students and journalists.
The violence continued until around 2 am. Around the same time, another group gathered outside Jadavpur police station and allegedly attempted to breach the entrance to the university’s main hostel, located next to the police station.
At the protest, ABVP West Bengal leaders were reportedly heard telling the media that the organisation was “putting the last nail in the coffin” of the “Dimagi Naxals” and would carry out “surgical strikes” at Jadavpur University to suppress them.
By around 2:30 am, the crowd had dispersed. The students who had taken shelter inside Aurobindo Bhavan began leaving the campus at around 5 am.
Alt News procured a third CCTV footage from University sources, where several persons of interest can be spotted as present on the campus on the night of August 20.
The confrontation did not end with the dispersal of the mob.
Around noon the following day, the Student Federation of India (SFI) and other Left student organisations held a protest near the Lenin statue at Jadavpur 8B bus stand. Kolkata Police barricaded the area and stopped the protesters from proceeding towards the university. Around 2 pm, an ABVP rally that began from Golpark reached Gate 4 of the university. Students inside the campus also gathered in response. As Gate 4 was kept locked to prevent outsiders from entering, a face-off between the two groups on either side of the gate ensued.
During the confrontation, members of the ABVP crowd were seen standing on the historic university emblem designed by artist Nandalal Bose as they attempted to cross the closed gate and enter the campus.
Visuals of Rajyeshwar Sinha, a professor of Bengali at JU, holding the partially damaged University emblem went viral.

ABVP Denial
Directly denying any role of ABVP, the outfit’s central working committee (CWC) member Subhabrata Adhikary said on a talk show on ABP Ananda, that ABVP had no connection with the rampage at Jadavpur University on August 20. When pointed out by the anchor that people in the mob were holding ABVP flags, Adhikary said, “It doesn’t prove anything. SFI workers have done the vandalism while holding ABVP flags”. When asked if ABVP was condemning the night-long violence, he again said, “It is clear that ABVP has no connection with the incident.”
Talking to The Times of India, south Bengal ABVP secretary Neelkantha Bhattacharya, too, denied his presence during the campus violence. However, he then said, some of ABVP boys entered the campus “out of over-enthusiasm. The gate was open. We just pushed inside. I went at most 10 steps inside the university to get them out”.
Adhikary, on the other hand, contradicted his own statement on ABP Ananda, and told TOI, “I was standing right by the gate. I have no connection with the mob. After hearing about the situation, I went there to ensure that no untoward incident happened. ABVP has no involvement in any vandalism.”
CCTV and Video Footage Disprove ABVP Claims
Alt News examined CCTV footage from the intervening night of August 19-20 and identified several prominent ABVP faces and BJP-linked political figures on the campus.
1. Subhabarta Adhikary
Visible in JU CCTV footage-1 (Captured by a camera fixed on the external wall of PG Arts building)
As the gate opens at 12.38.17 am, Adhikary is one of the first persons to enter the campus, followed by a crowd. When the group nears a large white SFI banner, he is seen saying something in an animated manner. Within seconds, others in the crowd tear down the banner. It is not clear whether he instructs them to do it or tries to dissuade them.
2. Neelkantha Bhattacharya
Visible in JU CCTV footage-2 (Captured by a camera installed on a pole at the science-arts crossing).
Around 12:40 am, Neelkantha Bhattacharya is seen carrying a rod or a stick while instructing a group. In the same footage, at the 12:39:22 am mark, Subhabrata Adhikary is seen next to him. They are in front of the PG science building. At 12:40:28, the two once again can be seen together. This time Bhattacharya is carrying sticks in both hands.
It is worth noting that Bhattacharyya first told TOI that he was not present on the campus. Then, he claimed, he had barely taken 10 steps inside the gate. The distance from Gate 4 to PG Science building, according to Google Maps, is over 360 feet, i.e., about 110 meters.
3. Somsurya Banerjee
Visible in JU CCTV footage-3 (Captured by a camera on the outer wall of security guards’ room at Gate-4)
Banerjee, an NSF activist, is spotted on the campus around 1.14 am on August 20. Banerjee had earlier courted controversy by claiming that cows were slaughtered within the University during Iftar.
4. Aditya Mondal
Visible in footage captured by Mrittika TV, a local media outlet.
The portal captured the exact moment when the crowd entered the campus, in a livestream. Although the video was later deleted from the page, Alt News accessed the footage. In that video, (embedded in the story above) Aditya Mondal, the ABVP candidate for the recently held election to internal complaint committee (ICC) of the Arts Faculty, was spotted near the PG science building. The wall had an SFI graffiti, where a person was seen urinating on the Nazi Hakenkreuz. The writing next to it said, ‘Break Fascism with Red’. Mondal was seen with a group that tried to rub the symbol off. Mondal can be heard saying, “The left-naxals had insulted the symbol of India, Swastik. We are correcting it.”
5. Partha Chakraborty
Visible in the footage captured by students stuck inside Aurobindo Bhavan, during the rampage.
Partha Chakraborty, a Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) worker from the Dhakuria area, was also present at the scene. In videos captured by the students stranded inside Aurobindo Bhavan, he was seen burning flags of SFI and other Left organizations in front of the collapsible gate of the building, and throwing the burning flags inside. Three days later, on August 23, he was seen with BJP’s losing candidate from Kasba assembly Sandeep Banerjee and South Kolkata Yuva Morcha leader Shatadru Ghoshal.
6. Abhijeet Roy (Raja)
Visible in JU CCTV footage-3 (Captured by a camera on the outer wall of security guards’ room at Gate-4)
Another prominent face identified in the footage from that night is Abhijeet Roy alias Raja, the election agent of Jadavpur MLA Sarbari Mukherjee. In a video posted on social media, Roy was seen standing with a group outside Gate-4, with one member holding an ABVP flag. ABVP leader Neelkantha Bhattacharya is part of the group. Roy’s entry into the campus was also captured on CCTV footage. He is seen interacting with a group of men with former VC Buddhadeb Sau standing at an arm’s length.
7. Buddhadeb Sau
Visible in JU CCTV footage-1 and JU CCTV footage-3.
The most talked about entry on that eventful night was perhaps that of Buddhadeb Sau, professor of mathematics and ex-VC of the university. Sau’s presence raised eyebrows not only for the fact that it is unusual for an academic of his stature to be on the campus past midnight, but also because of his Sangh connections. He is associated with the RSS-backed Akhil Bhartiya Rashtriya Shaikshik Mahasangh (ABRSM), and represented the organisation at a joint press meet held by Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh JU unit, ABVP JU unit and ABRSM JU unit, held after the campus violence.
Sau can be spotted in JU CCTV footage-1 and JU CCTV footage-3. In the JU CCTV footage-1 feed, he is seen entering the campus through a side gate at 12:39:44 am, and exiting through the same gate at 12:44:35 am. For the entire duration, he stood in front of the security guards’ room, occasionally speaking to others. From 12:44:09 till his exit 26 seconds later, he is seen watching others tearing down what appears to be political flags put up on Gate-4.
